newsitem.title: INDONESIA: China seeks lasting relations with Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: China seeks lasting relations with Indonesia.

text.p: Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian said on Thursday Beijing was willing to develop lasting relations with Indonesia and promote peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific region.
"China is willing to develop lasting and stable relations of friendship and cooperation with Indonesia," Chi said on his arrival from Manila for a five-day visit to Indonesia.
He continued his trip despite the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping. Indonesian President Suharto, on a state visit to Laos, has expressed the country's condolences over Deng's death.

Chi said exchanges and cooperation between China and Indonesia had expanded and strengthened in various fields and relations between the two militaries had developed steadily since diplomatic relations were normalised in 1990.
"This not only conforms to the common interests and aspirations of our two peoples, but also is conducive to peace and stability of the Asia-Pacific region," he said.
Indonesia resumed diplomatic ties with China in 1990 after severing them following a 1965 coup attempt blamed on the Indonesian Communist Party (PKI), which is still officially banned.
Chi's itinerary includes meetings with his host, Defence Minister Edi Sudradjat, and with Suharto following his return from Burma, the last leg of the president's Southeast Asian trip, on Sunday.
